description: The left diagram is labeled “Ideal structure: perfect binary tree.” Root 1 has left child 2 and right child 3. Node 2 has left child 4 and right child 5, and 3 has left child 6 and right child 7. All four bottom nodes, 4, 5, 6, and 7, are leaves. There are 3 levels, and the path from root 1 to any leaf crosses just 2 edges, so the height is 2.

The right diagram is labeled “Degenerate structure: linked list.” All 7 nodes lean left, with left child pointers forming the chain 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7. Every right child is empty. There are 7 levels, and the path from root 1 to the only leaf, 7, crosses 6 edges, giving a height of 6.

frames.explanation: When every level is full, the perfect binary tree has minimum height and can take advantage of divide and conquer. When all nodes lean to one side and form a linked list, the tree reaches maximum height and operations along a path take linear time.
frames.title: Ideal and chain-shaped binary trees

summary: The same seven nodes can form trees of different heights depending on whether they branch or all connect on one side.
title: Ideal and chain-shaped binary trees
